observationHints: Note the position of the second-last defender at the moment the ball is played, arm position relative to the body (is it making the body unnaturally bigger?), and whether contact by a defender preceded the attacker playing the ball.

rules.title: Offside Position
rules.text: A player is in an offside position if: any part of the head, body or feet is in the opponents' half (excluding the halfway line) and any part of the head, body or feet is nearer to the opponents' goal line than both the ball and the second-last opponent.

source.label: IFAB Laws of the Game — Law 11.1: Offside position

rules.title: Offside Offence - Interfering
rules.text: A player in an offside position at the moment the ball is played or touched by a team-mate is only penalised on becoming involved in active play by: interfering with play by playing or touching a ball passed or touched by a team-mate, or interfering with an opponent.

source.label: IFAB Laws of the Game — Law 11.2: Offside offence

rules.title: Fair Tackle (Playing the Ball)
rules.text: A tackle is fair if the defender makes contact with the ball before making contact with the attacker, provided the tackle is not careless, reckless, or using excessive force. If the defender wins the ball cleanly and subsequent unavoidable contact occurs, it is generally not a foul.

source.label: IFAB Laws of the Game — Law 12.1: Direct free kick

rules.title: Direct Free Kick - Careless Challenge
rules.text: A direct free kick is awarded if a player tackles or challenges an opponent in a manner considered to be careless. 'Careless' means the player shows a lack of attention or consideration when making a challenge or acts without precaution. No disciplinary sanction (card) is needed. E.g., tripping an opponent by missing the ball.

source.label: IFAB Laws of the Game — Law 12.1: Direct free kick

rules.title: Direct Free Kick - Reckless Challenge (Yellow Card)
rules.text: A direct free kick is awarded if a player acts with disregard to the danger to, or consequences for, an opponent. This is considered 'reckless' and the player must be cautioned (yellow card). E.g., a sliding tackle with studs showing that hits the opponent's ankle/foot.

source.label: IFAB Laws of the Game — Law 12.1: Direct free kick

rules.title: Direct Free Kick - Excessive Force (Red Card)
rules.text: A direct free kick is awarded if a player exceeds the necessary use of force and endangers the safety of an opponent. This is 'using excessive force' and the player must be sent off (red card). E.g., a high-speed lunge with studs striking above the ankle.

source.label: IFAB Laws of the Game — Law 12.1: Direct free kick

rules.title: Handling the ball - Deliberate
rules.text: It is an offence if a player deliberately touches the ball with their hand/arm, for example moving the hand/arm towards the ball.

source.label: IFAB Laws of the Game — Law 12.1: Direct free kick

rules.title: Handling the ball - Unnaturally Bigger
rules.text: It is an offence if a player touches the ball with their hand/arm when it has made their body unnaturally bigger. A player is considered to have made their body unnaturally bigger when the position of their hand/arm is not a consequence of, or justifiable by, the player's body movement for that specific situation.

source.label: IFAB Laws of the Game — Law 12.1: Direct free kick

rules.title: Handling the ball - Exceptions
rules.text: It is not an offence if the ball touches a player's hand/arm: directly from the player's own head or body; directly from the head or body of another player who is close; if the hand/arm is close to the body and does not make the body unnaturally bigger; when a player falls and the hand/arm is between the body and the ground to support the body.

source.label: IFAB Laws of the Game — Law 12.1: Direct free kick

rules.title: Simulation (Dive)
rules.text: Attempts to deceive the referee e.g. by feigning injury or pretending to have been fouled (simulation) must be sanctioned as unsporting behaviour which is an offence punishable by a yellow card.

source.label: IFAB Laws of the Game — Law 12: Fouls and Misconduct, Disciplinary action

rules.title: The Penalty Kick
rules.text: A penalty kick is awarded if a player commits a direct free kick offence inside their penalty area or off the field as part of play as outlined in Laws 12 and 13.

source.label: IFAB Laws of the Game — Law 14: The Penalty Kick

rules.title: Holding an opponent
rules.text: A direct free kick is awarded if a player holds an opponent.

source.label: IFAB Laws of the Game — Law 12.1: Direct free kick

rules.title: Impeding with contact
rules.text: A direct free kick is awarded if a player impedes an opponent with contact.

source.label: IFAB Laws of the Game — Law 12.1: Direct free kick

rules.title: Impeding without contact
rules.text: An indirect free kick is awarded if a player impedes the progress of an opponent without any contact being made.

source.label: IFAB Laws of the Game — Law 12.2: Indirect free kick

rules.title: Offside Offence - Gaining an advantage
rules.text: A player in an offside position is penalised if they gain an advantage by playing the ball or interfering with an opponent when it has rebounded or been deflected off the goalpost, crossbar, match official or an opponent, or has been deliberately saved by any opponent.

source.label: IFAB Laws of the Game — Law 11.2: Offside offence
